_comment: NEVER COMMIT THIS FILE. Access credentials and resource definitions.

servers._comment: Key-based auth only. There is deliberately no password field — a plaintext password in this file would be read by every skill and echoed into run logs. Use ssh_key_path; if a host only takes passwords, add it to ~/.ssh/config with a key instead.

compute._comment: Rented compute providers. `lease.py` discovers adapters by filename and treats a provider as usable only when it has a block here — installing `provider_x.py` is not the same as declaring you have an account. Owned machines are NOT here: they live in `servers` above and are reached through the `ssh` adapter, which self-registers off that block. Nothing downstream branches on which of the two a machine came from; see `.claude/skills/lease/references/contract.md`.
compute._comment_no_ids: ‼️ No tenant, project, subnet or image id belongs in any of these blocks, and none is needed: every adapter discovers its own scope from the credential at call time. Ids drift, a pinned one points somewhere wrong in silence, and the first trap in the contract's 'Scope completeness' is exactly that failure. What lives here is preference and local paths.

_example_nebius._comment_regions: `allow_regions` narrows every scope walk. Leave empty to search everywhere; set it to keep a fleet in the region where the data bucket lives, since an out-of-region box pays cross-region egress on every pull and waits on it. `project_name` picks between several projects in the same region and is a name, not an id.
_example_nebius._comment_credential: Nebius auth is federated (SSO) and the token is short-lived — the adapter declares `credential_ttl_s` and Money rule 5 refuses a job longer than it. The OAuth refresh cannot complete headlessly, so an unattended run whose token expires cannot reach, monitor, or destroy its own boxes.

local._comment_env_manager: How a run enters the right Python env. `tool`: pixi | mamba | conda | uv, detected by /resources in that preference order. pixi is preferred where present because its env is keyed to a project directory and a lockfile — an env it resolves is reconstructible from the repo, where a named conda env is a machine's local state that may simply be gone. /repro's env axis can only report drift against what was captured; a lockfile is the only form that lets somebody rebuild it.

outsourcing._comment: Parties work is sent to and comes back from — annotation vendors, data owners, reviewers, customers. This is the /data-label analogue of `servers`: a route to a capability MLClaw doesn't own, recorded once and reused across every batch. Workspace-level for the same reason servers are — a vendor is not project-specific, and their turnaround and rate are facts about them, not about one batch. Contact details are personal data, and this file is the one that is never committed; that is why they live here and are never copied into a project's handoff records, which are git-tracked. Handoff records store the key only, and contact is resolved live at report time — the same rule as /lease 'never write a resolved address into a config file'.
